preamble: Lenition of the labiodental fricative [v] to the labial-velar approximant [w]. In Belarusian, /v/ in the syllable coda becomes [w]~[u̯], written ў, as in праўда 'truth' (compare Russian правда). Early 19th-century London Cockney had a well-known interchange of v and w, as in Dickens's Sam Weller saying 'wery' for 'very'.

examples.note: Coda /v/ forms a diphthong with the preceding vowel, e.g. праўда [ˈprawda] 'truth' against Russian правда [ˈpravdə]. Some ў, as in воўк [vɔwk] 'wolf', come from /l/ instead.
The v/w interchange of East End speech, represented by Dickens in The Pickwick Papers (1836), where the reverse substitution ('avay' for 'away') also occurs; it had died out by the late 19th century.
